title: Markets Look Calm… But Something Feels Off... ft. Rob Carver - Systematic Investor - Ep.396

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Markets Look Calm… But Something Feels Off... ft. Rob Carver - Systematic Investor - Ep.396.docx

summary: Carver and Kaastrup-Larsen discuss April 2026 markets (Iran war oil shock, CTA performance), Carver's 12-month review favoring slow trend, and the Quantica return-stacking paper and managed-futures ETF article. Conclusions: simple robust methods, cost focus, diversifiers judged by correlation and cash efficiency.

coverage.note: intro, scam warning for CTA impersonation, AI audiobook chat
war, muted equities, oil futures vs physical disconnect
oil, S&P record, UCITS ETF performance fee
UK ETF wrappers, Bessent, trend barometer
April CTA index numbers, Carver risk level and positions
Carver 12-month review, benchmarks, signals
signals review: slow trend, carry, skew, costs
London CTA due diligence, AHL lineage, style differences
marginal gains, due diligence on process
PhDs, simplicity, AI risk
slow research cycle, tedious work, PhD roles
diversity of thought, same weights across instruments
pooling fitting, crisis alpha objective, joint optimisation
Quantica paper stack it, return stacking
cash efficiency of futures
correlation, drag, efficiency, allocation limits
Sharpe not key, gold sample, forward-looking returns
gold vs inflation, Dunn study, RPM ETF article intro
ETF correlation, simplification tax, performance
poor man's CTA, crisis alpha measurement
adjusting replication comparison, interest income
outro and disclaimer

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: there is this substantial supply shock happening um in in um in oil.
claims.claim: Equity markets showed a muted reaction to a large oil supply shock from the war, which Carver expects to matter eventually.
claims.direction: expects equities to be hit when the shock feeds through
claims.conditions: Carver says the rubber will hit the road at some point
claims.testable: partly: needs a defined shock and reaction window

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the price of physical oil, um which is seems to have become quite disconnected from the price of uh futures
claims.claim: Physical oil prices can decouple from benchmark futures (WTI, Brent) in a supply shock, so futures understate the squeeze.
claims.conditions: futures at 90-100 dollars while physical is far higher in some locations
claims.testable: partly: physical spot data by location is hard to obtain

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: where your oil is, and where it's being delivered to, is extremely important
claims.claim: A physical-delivery futures contract is tied to a specified grade and delivery location, so futures and local spot prices can diverge.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: physical price of oil in Sri Lanka at the moment is, and I feel like a dramatic pause is is required here, $286 a barrel
claims.claim: Named number: physical oil in Sri Lanka at 286 dollars a barrel, more than three times the futures price, shows the futures/physical disconnect.
claims.testable: partly: source is an FT Alphaville article

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: even $100 a barrel doesn't really accurately reflect, you know, what what the sort of pent-up demand and lack of supply for oil is is going to be
claims.claim: Carver thinks 100 dollars oil understates the pent-up demand and lack of supply, so more upside is possible.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the S&P 500 closed at a new all-time high yesterday, like nothing's going on in the world
claims.claim: The S&P 500 hit a new all-time high after roughly a 10 percent correction, a quick dip-buying recovery despite the war.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: performance fees, at least in theory, do provide a better alignment of incentives between investors and managers
claims.claim: Performance fees better align managers with investors than flat fees paid for raising assets.
claims.testable: partly: compare fund fee structures to returns

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: You're really restricted to either buying shares or buying ETFs.
claims.claim: UK tax-sheltered accounts (ISAs, SIPPs) limit holdings to shares and ETFs, creating demand for ETF versions of CTA strategies despite platform fees.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: They should wait and see before deciding whether to lower interest rates
claims.claim: Treasury Secretary Bessent said the Fed should wait and see on rate cuts during the Iranian war, giving mixed signals with the White House.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: My own trend barometer finished at 55 yesterday which is pretty strong.
claims.claim: Kaastrup's trend barometer, a gauge of aggregate CTA trend strength, read 55 (strong) after the equity rebound and metals recovery.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: managers with longer term time frames and who may not have well, they would have reduced their exposure I'm sure in March but they may not have gotten short equities
claims.claim: Longer-horizon trend followers reduced equity exposure in March without going short, so they gained from the April equity rebound.
claims.direction: slower trend benefits in whipsaw rebound

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the Beta 50 was up 51 basis points in April up 8.03% so far this year
claims.claim: Named data: CTA indices (Beta 50, SG CTA, SG Trend) up about 8 percent YTD versus MSCI World +4.07 percent.
claims.indicator: Beta 50; SG CTA Index; SG Trend Index; MSCI World

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: metals. They're back in favor again. And and some of the currency some of the I think resource country type currencies are doing pretty well.
claims.claim: In April metals and resource-country currencies resumed trending up, helping trend followers.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: my current risk level running at about a third of my kind of long-term targets
claims.claim: Carver's vol-targeted system cuts risk to a third of target when forecasts are weak, so risk scales with signal strength.
claims.testable: yes: compare scaled vs fixed risk

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: long long equities short short bonds is kind of inflationary
claims.claim: Carver's positions: modest long equities, small long energy, larger short bonds, an inflation-leaning mix that may net flat if the oil shock hits equities.
claims.direction: long equities, long energy, short bonds

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: in my futures trading I made drum roll please 23.7%
claims.claim: Carver made 23.7 percent in his futures account over the April-to-April UK tax year, mostly in two bursts.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: sort of now famous kind of metals bubble which we talked about actually in the last podcast I think in terms of position sizing
claims.claim: Position sizing in vol-targeted trend following mechanically takes profit out of a metals bubble as volatility rises.
claims.conditions: violent metals spike late Dec to early Jan
claims.testable: yes: simulate sizing rules on silver

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I look at that just on an outright basis but also on a vol adjusted basis cuz my vol is quite a lot higher than theirs
claims.claim: When benchmarking a trader against CTA indices, compare both raw and volatility-adjusted returns, since risk targets differ.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: it's more of a it's kind of more of a direct comparison if you like cuz it means there's less sort of currency related noise
claims.claim: Choose a benchmark denominated in the same currency as the account to remove currency noise.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: After the vol adjustment actually they're slightly ahead of me.
claims.claim: After volatility adjustment the AHL fund and SG CTA index (about 30 percent each) slightly beat Carver's roughly 26 percent.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: pure trend following did better than than the other signals that I have in my portfolio which I have a more higher weight to
claims.claim: A multi-signal book (trend plus carry, skew) lags pure trend in a good trend year but protected in the terrible prior year.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: some of my best performing, um, asset classes were equities which and metals
claims.claim: Over the 12 months equities and metals contributed most and bonds lost most, so a bond-focused CTA had a hard year.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: it had a a fairly decent trend upwards for most of the year up to about October
claims.claim: Feeder cattle gave a smooth trend and re-entry opportunities, whereas silver was a violent move, so smoother trends are easier to trade.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: what I call my core momentum signal which is just literally, um, exponentially weighted moving average crossovers
claims.claim: Carver's core EWMAC divergent trend signal was the best of his divergent rules in the past year.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I can't see a single place where um, even even if you ignore costs where my very fastest uh, signals did better than my much slower ones
claims.claim: The slowest trend signals did best in every case, even before costs, making it a good year to be overallocated to slow trend following.
claims.conditions: one year, prolonged trends with sharp reversals

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: carry was kind of flat maybe slightly down. Um, relative carry was up a little bit.
claims.claim: Convergent signals: carry flat, relative carry slightly positive over the past year.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: looks for markets where there's been uh, you know, effectively recent fat negative tails and then buys them
claims.claim: A skew-based convergent signal buys markets with recent fat negative tails, a bounce strategy, and it added value.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: performance is random. Costs are not. Costs are very predictable from year to year and very consistent.
claims.claim: Costs are predictable while performance is noise, so give costs more weight in design than performance.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: my costs are exactly in line where I'd expect them to be
claims.claim: Realised slippage and costs were within one or two basis points of the prior year, validating the cost model.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: to a large extent the successful ones, um, to to to some degree uh, actually use more or less the same methodology
claims.claim: Many large London CTAs share the AHL origin and similar methodology.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: unlike uh, the US methodology which was more kind of breakout style either vol or price breakout
claims.claim: European CTAs use moving-average / time-series momentum, US CTAs historically breakouts.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: So, it it comes down to speed, methodology, markets universe.
claims.claim: CTAs differ mainly in speed, methodology details and the markets traded, not core method.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: you can knock 50 basis points off your slippage you might think that's not very much but actually that's 50 basis points pretty much guaranteed every year forever
claims.claim: Marginal gains: cutting 50bp of slippage is a near-certain annual gain, whereas 50bp of expected return is random.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: diversifying through adding lots of markets for example making sure you're not trading the not markets too quickly making sure you've got accurate estimates of costs making sure you haven't over fitted
claims.claim: Small robust improvements add up: wide diversification, not trading too fast, accurate costs and avoiding overfit.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I'd be asking them quite tedious questions about you know things like operational processes and cost estimation
claims.claim: In CTA due diligence ask about operations and cost estimation, not the source of alpha.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: people who are very smart tend to have a preference for simpler things.
claims.claim: Experienced quants prefer simple methods and know when they suffice.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: tend to use more complex methods almost for the sake of using more complex methods
claims.claim: Inexperienced highly qualified people overuse complexity (e.g. over naive mean-variance), which can worsen results.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: nothing more dangerous than someone using a a more complex mathematical method that they don't really understand what it's doing
claims.claim: Using complex methods without understanding them is the main danger.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: maybe only 0.01% of people using these in financial data are actually doing it in a way that that's not going to go horribly wrong
claims.claim: Most uses of AI/LLMs on financial data go wrong because users do not understand them.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the research cycle is quite long so you can use the same model for years potentially decades
claims.claim: Slow trading means little alpha decay, so one model can run for years without a large research team finding new signals.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: they're tedious things like properly measuring your your transaction costs
claims.claim: Performance gains come from tedious work: measuring costs and cleaning data to diversify into more markets.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if you're going to start trading options as well as futures well clearly you need people who understand how options are priced and how to build wall surfaces
claims.claim: PhD-level skills are needed when diversifying into options, equities or HFT.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: very smart people have a tendency to focus on things that they find sort of intellectually interesting and then overlook the the the sort of boring stuff
claims.claim: Quant managers must keep researchers on unglamorous but valuable work.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: long-term performance has been better than firms with as you say 50 PhDs
claims.claim: Dunn's long-term performance with 1-2 PhDs beat firms with 50, so team size does not drive results.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: it's probably not spending much time on signal generation. It's probably all the other things including risk management
claims.claim: Most quant staff effort in CTAs goes to risk management and other infrastructure, not signals.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I do actually basically assume that all instruments are the same as far as fitting goes.
claims.claim: Use identical forecast weights for every instrument to avoid overfitting.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: you'd then essentially pull your fitting across those two assets and you and use the sort of joint information between them
claims.claim: Plan: statistically test whether instrument weights differ, then pool fitting across similar instruments such as US 5 and 10 year.
claims.conditions: only allow differing weights with statistical evidence

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if all of your money was just in trend following and you had no other investments at all, then you definitely wouldn't do this
claims.claim: Optimise a CTA for crisis alpha only if it is a sleeve in a larger portfolio, otherwise maximise Sharpe.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: reduce your risk weighting in equities and bonds in the CTA sleeve because you already have an exposure in the other parts of your portfolio
claims.claim: Jointly optimising a portfolio cuts equity and bond weights in the CTA sleeve, adds ags and speeds it up.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: you'd want maybe more like trend in equities than carry because you want that sort of responsiveness of to sell-offs of equity
claims.claim: For crisis alpha, weight trend over carry in equities for fast response to sell-offs.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you don't necessarily have to sell your equities in order to benefit from having some trend following exposure
claims.claim: Equity investors can add trend following on top via portable alpha/return stacking without selling equities.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: you have it's like a piece of pizza and you have to kind of cut the pizza up into slices and you you know so would it be 60% in in equities 40% in bonds
claims.claim: Allocation is buying risk with cash, so leverage can enlarge the pie instead of slicing a fixed one.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: 25% cash to get 15% vol is is an extremely efficient you know you use of cash
claims.claim: Futures need about 25 percent cash for 15 percent vol (Carver 30-35 percent at 25 vol), enabling stacking.
claims.conditions: due to futures leverage, not trend following

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the three things determining what your optimal portfolio is going to be the correlations we've discussed lower the better
claims.claim: Optimal size of an added strategy depends on correlation to equities, diversification drag and cash efficiency.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: you can actually convert those into higher returns by sort of whacking your leverage up again as long as you don't you don't get too crazy
claims.claim: Leverage converts diversification's higher Sharpe into higher return despite lower raw return.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: because it's correlation to equities is actually negative you can actually have a an allocation that's over 100% theoretically theoretically
claims.claim: Quantica result: short vol should be about 10 percent of an equity portfolio, long vol over 100 percent.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: trend following gold or treasuries which also kind of sit in the middle you can kind of stick 50% of your portfolio quite happily
claims.claim: Trend following, gold and Treasuries can take about 50 percent allocations alongside equities.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: It really isn't about finding something with a high sharp ratio. It's finding something that behaves differently that allows you and and is cash efficient
claims.claim: Choose diversifiers by low correlation and cash efficiency rather than high Sharpe.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: gold futures would have a produced a cumulative return of negative 53%
claims.claim: Gold's strong stats depend on the sample period; 1990s gold futures lost 53 percent, so test earlier periods.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: just assume that all assets have the same sharp ratio for example you know forward-looking
claims.claim: Use equal forward-looking Sharpe ratios for assets in allocation rather than extrapolating the equity run.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: in equities it's not unreasonable to expect to that you you'd earn sort of price earnings ratio with a sort of inflation component attached to it
claims.claim: Fundamental return expectations: equities earn earnings yield plus inflation.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: my long-term forecast for gold is I'd say well probably just inflation plus zero because it doesn't it doesn't earn anything
claims.claim: Gold should return inflation plus zero because supply responds to price.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if you kind of plot an inflation line the gold will have just gone around that with big swings of course huge
claims.claim: Gold swings widely around an inflation-adjusted trend over 50 years.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: given its return is should be systematically lower than say equities bonds or dare I say CTAs then that allocation should be relatively low
claims.claim: Gold, with lower expected return, merits only a small allocation.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there's really only one standing and that is trend following
claims.claim: Dunn study: among alternatives to combine with equities, only trend following stands out (author is biased).

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if you were to choose 13 random CTAs actual funds rather than ETFs and look at their correlations you'd probably find they were quite similar
claims.claim: Judge ETF correlation to SG CTA by comparing with correlation of random actual CTAs.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: tracking error or um perhaps let's call it a simplification tax
claims.claim: Replication ETFs trade off cost savings against a simplification tax from limited contracts.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: some of the numbers thrown around in terms of cost savings seem, you know, seem a little bit large given that um you know, you potentially still have to trade the thing
claims.claim: Claimed cost savings of replication look overstated.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: roughly speaking um the performance is not massively out of line with a SocGen ETF
claims.claim: Managed futures ETFs (13 US funds, 10 years) performed similarly to the SG index.
claims.indicator: managed futures ETFs vs SG CTA

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: none of these funds are doing a terrible job
claims.claim: ETFs are reasonable as a poor man's CTA; no evidence either way versus real CTAs.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: they do measure crisis alpha. Um but I'm not sure exactly how they calculate it
claims.claim: Crisis alpha needs a clear definition (episodes or threshold decline); the study doesn't say.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: there just haven't been enough crises to say for sure whether a given type of fund is likely to provide you know, a better or worse crisis alpha
claims.claim: Ten years has too few crises to compare crisis alpha across funds.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the index that is often used to compare to replication CTAs does not include 100% interest income
claims.claim: Compare replication to CTAs only after adjusting for vol and interest income.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: once you adjust for these things and maybe once you uh use a more appropriate um such as the SocGen Trend Index there has been no outperformance uh by replication uh CTAs
claims.claim: After adjustment, replication CTAs show no outperformance.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if you simplify the strategy you kind of remove the edge that the investor is buying it for
claims.claim: Simplification removes the edge; replication is very slow.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: basis points came purely just from interest income on my margin
claims.claim: About 300bp of Carver's 12-month return was interest on margin, so including it matters.
